# Visual and diagram instructions

- Start with the communication goal and intended audience; do not add decorative visuals without instructional value.
- Use consistent labels, terminology, directionality, boundaries, legends, and readable contrast.
- Network diagrams must show trust zones, interfaces/segments, relevant IP ranges, traffic direction, and major data flows where known.
- Do not invent network addresses, firewall behavior, event flow, or component capabilities.
- Keep source/editable diagram assets when the format supports them; document any export/rendering steps.
- Provide text descriptions or accessible labels for important visual information.
- Check layout at typical presentation and document sizes; avoid tiny text and ambiguous connectors.
- Identify whether a visual is conceptual, proposed, documented, or validated.


## Bilingual authoring requirements

- Arabic and English are first-class project languages. Follow `governance/policies/bilingual-content-policy.md`.
- Keep paired documents in the same directory; English uses the canonical filename and Arabic appends `-ar` before the extension.
- Preserve stable IDs, technical meaning, commands, code, SPL, field names, configuration keys, numeric values, safety boundaries, evidence, and assessment requirements.
- Update both language variants together when meaning changes, or mark the counterpart `needs-update`/pending. Do not claim parity without reviewing both.
